     9	# The Abel-compatibility square demands nothing, and its consumer is circular
    10	
    11	Roadmap `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j` records DAT-J as owing **three** things, the first being
    12	
    13	> 1. `IsAbelClassifyCompatible` for the campaign's Abel morphism — bookkeeping-shaped, but a
    14	>    real statement, and nobody has written it;
    15	
    16	with the fibrewise Riemann–Roch effectivity input `heff` as a *separate* item 2.  **That
    17	partition does not survive contact with the interface**, and this file measures why in Lean
    18	rather than in prose.
    19	
    20	## The measurement
    21	
    22	`IsAbelClassifyCompatible … abel pt` takes the point map `pt` as an **argument**, not as
    23	fixed data.  So a consumer entitled to choose `pt` can choose it to be the classifier
    24	composite itself, and the square becomes `dif_pos` — for an **arbitrary** `abel`, over an
    25	arbitrary curve, with no geometry whatsoever:
    26	
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAbelClassifyCompatible` below. Its only hypothesis beyond
    28	  `abel` is that the `pt` *type* is inhabited at all (`pt0`), which supplies the junk branch
    29	  of the case split.
    30	
    31	So obligation 1 is not "bookkeeping-shaped but real".  It is **free**, in the precise sense
    32	that `∃ pt, IsAbelClassifyCompatible … abel pt` is a theorem.  This is the recorded
    33	"isolating a residue as a class" failure mode (inbox `I-0605`): a residue whose witness is
    34	existentially quantified over the very datum that would make it non-trivial demands nothing,
    35	and the cheap test is to try to inhabit it with junk **before** treating it as a reduction.
    36	
    37	## The consequence for the consumer, which is the part that matters
    38	
    39	`exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean`) consumes
    40	`pt`, `hsq` and `heff` and concludes
    41	
    42	> `∀ y, ∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = J.fromSpecResidueField y`.
    43	
    44	Instantiate it at the `pt` produced above and read `heff`: it asks for a `D` with
    45	`pt κ(y) D = J.fromSpecResidueField y`, which at that `pt` unfolds to
    46	`(classify D).left ≫ abel = J.fromSpecResidueField y` — **verbatim the conclusion**.  So at
    47	the `pt` that makes `hsq` free, the theorem is a tautology: `heff` has silently absorbed all
    48	of the content that item 1 appeared to carry.  `exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible`
    49	is therefore a *reduction only relative to a `pt` pinned independently* — pinned to the
    50	campaign Abel map's own point map — and the interface never pins it.
    51	
    52	`heff_iff_conclusion_of_pt_eq` records that circularity as a lemma, so the claim is
    53	machine-checked and not an argument in a docstring.
    54	
    55	## What DAT-J actually owes, restated
    56	
    57	**One** statement, not two, and it is strictly stronger than the "Riemann–Roch over a field"
    58	that item 2 describes: for every point `y` of `J`, an effective degree-`g` divisor on the
    59	curve over `κ(y)` **whose classifying morphism composes with `abel` to `fromSpecResidueField
    60	y`**.  The Riemann–Roch half produces the divisor; the compatibility half is the honest
    61	residue, and it cannot be split off into a separate row because any `pt` making the split
    62	statable is either the pinned campaign one (in which case there is no separate row to prove)
    63	or a chosen one (in which case the split is vacuous).
    64	
    65	Spelling of the Riemann–Roch half stays binding per `informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md` §0.5:
    66	`exists_effective_of_picClass` / `riemann_inequality`, **never** `riemann_inequality_curve`
    67	(it imports `Challenge.lean` and would create an import cycle).
    68	
    69	## What this does NOT do
    70	
    71	It produces no lift, no `JacobianData`, and no effectivity witness — it **removes a row**
    72	from DAT-J's ledger by showing that row was free, and relocates its content onto the row
    73	that was already there.  Critical-path §7.6 (L8) is untouched.
    74	
    75	## Main declarations
    76	
    77	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAbelClassifyCompatible` — the square is satisfiable for an
    78	  arbitrary `abel`: obligation 1 of the `dat-j` row is vacuous.
    79	* `AlgebraicGeometry.heff_iff_conclusion_of_pt_eq` — at such a `pt`, the remaining
    80	  hypothesis `heff` is equivalent to the conclusion it was supposed to imply.
    81	-/

   154	Read against the `dat-j` roadmap row, which lists `IsAbelClassifyCompatible` as a real

   158	    (pt0 : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
   159	      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   160	      [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))],
   161	      (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J)) :
   162	    ∃ pt, IsAbelClassifyCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 abel pt := by
   163	  classical
   164	  refine ⟨abelClassifyPt hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 abel pt0, ?_⟩

   170	    else pt0 K D)

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-J step 3 is one compatibility square, not a construction
    11	
    12	`Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean` reduced DAT-J to two inputs: a
    13	`PicRepDatum k k C` and, for every point `y` of the representing object, a lift
    14	
    15	> `∃ q : Spec κ(y) ⟶ DivScheme g, q ≫ abel = fromSpecResidueField y`.
    16	
    17	The lift has been read as "the Abel map is surjective on points", i.e. as geometry still
    18	to be done. **The morphism half is already built**, in a rooted file, and what is missing
    19	is only that it sits over the right point.
    20	
    21	## What is landed, and had no consumer
    22	
    23	`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean` (rooted, sorry-free) carries the whole *fibrewise*
    24	chain, and the reason it is short is that **over a field the certificate is free**:
    25	
    26	* `DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg` (`:104`) — over a field `K`, an adaptation whose
    27	  presentation divisor has degree `n` is `IsCertified n`.  All seven clauses: projectivity
    28	  and both flat-cokernel clauses are `Module.Free.of_divisionRing` instances, `(c1)`
    29	  finiteness is `moduleFinite_colength`, and the `(c2)` rank clause is the *unconditional*
    30	  CRT identity `deg_presentationDivisor` read against the degree hypothesis.  No support
    31	  separation is needed — which the file records as a deviation of record, since full
    32	  support separation is unachievable when a support point lies in both charts' overlap.
    33	* `exists_divFam_divFamDivisor_eq` (`:147`) — hence every effective degree-`g` divisor over
    34	  `K` *is* the divisor of a `DivFam`.
    35	* `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar` (`:217`) — and it classifies, giving
    36	  `overSpec k K ⟶ divSchemeOver …`, characterized by `effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec`
    37	  (`:231`).
    38	
    39	This is the sharp form of critical-path §7.6's own observation that the `DivFamZar` no-go
    40	is a purely *relative* phenomenon, **vacuous over a field**: the difficulty that makes U2
    41	hard does not exist fibrewise.
    42	
    43	## What is therefore actually missing
    44	
    45	`effectiveDivisorClassifyZar_spec` says the morphism is `divRepClassifyZar` of a family
    46	presenting `D`.  It says **nothing about `abel`**.  So joining it to `hlift` needs exactly
    47	one statement — that classifying an effective divisor and then applying the Abel map
    48	returns the class of that divisor's point:
    49	
    50	> `AbelCompatible abel` : for every field point and every effective degree-`g` divisor `D`
    51	> over it, `(effectiveDivisorClassifyZar … D …).left ≫ abel` is the morphism `Spec K ⟶ J`
    52	> named by the class of `D`.
    53	
    54	That is a *compatibility square*, not a surjectivity theorem, and it is the recorded
    55	"groups agree ≠ maps agree" gap (inbox `I-0525`): a bijection between divisor classes and
    56	`DivScheme`-points is unusable until the square relating the two named morphisms lands.
    57	
    58	## Main declarations
    59	
    60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAbelClassifyCompatible` — the square, as a named interface.
    61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_residueField_lift_of_abelCompatible` — the square plus
    62	  fibrewise effectivity gives the `hlift` obligation **verbatim** as
    63	  `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` / `PicRepDatum.toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts` consume it.
    64	
    65	## What this does NOT do
    66	
    67	It produces no `AbelClassifyCompatible` and no effectivity witness, so it builds no
    68	`JacobianData`.  It removes the *construction* from DAT-J step 3 and leaves a square and
    69	an effectivity input, both stated here rather than assumed anywhere.
    70	
    71	## AMENDMENT 2026-07-29: `heff` is NOT the divRep-gated half
    72	
    73	The text above calls `heff` "the honest geometric input", which is right, and the `dat-j`
    74	roadmap row read that as work still gated behind divisor representability.  It is not:
    75	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean` and `Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`
    76	discharge the effectivity content, at every point of *any* `Pic⁰`-representing object, with
    77	no `divFunctor`, no `DivFamZar`, no certificate and no chart
    78	(`exists_effective_deg_eq_of_pic0_at_point`).
    79	
    80	So of the two halves this file separates, only the **square** is divRep-gated — naming
    81	`abel` requires the representation.  They were never gated alike.  What the effectivity side
    82	still owes is *descent*: its divisor lives over a finite separable splitting field of `κ(y)`,
    83	and `hlift` wants `Spec κ(y)` itself.
    84	-/

   133	
   134	/-- **The Abel-compatibility square** — the one statement standing between the landed
   135	fibrewise classification and DAT-J's `hlift` obligation.
   136	
   137	At a scheme `J` and a morphism `abel : DivScheme g ⟶ J`, this says: whenever a point `y`

   139	residue field — presented in the sense that the classifying morphism composed with `abel`

   167	square.  Note what is *not* here: no surjectivity of the Abel map on points is proved, and
   168	no divisor is produced — `heff` is the honest geometric input (Riemann–Roch: a degree-`g`
   169	class on a curve of genus `g` over a field has an effective representative, to be spelled
   170	with `exists_effective_of_picClass` / `riemann_inequality` and **never** with
   171	`riemann_inequality_curve`, which imports `Challenge.lean`). -/

   173	    (pt : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
   174	      [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   175	      [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))],
   176	      (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor → (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ J))
   177	    (hsq : IsAbelClassifyCompatible hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 abel pt)
   178	    (heff : ∀ y : J, ∃ (_ : Algebra k (J.residueField y))
   179	      (_ : IsIntegral (relCurve C (J.residueField y)))
   180	      (_ : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
   181	        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))
   182	      (_ : QuasiCompact
   183	        (relCurve C (J.residueField y) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of (J.residueField y))))

Granting a representation
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff}(C,n)\text{ is represented by }D\), and separately supplying a
  chart family of relatively representable open immersions together with the required
  locally-surjective \(\Sigma\)-map, the widened Abel chart
  \(\operatorname{abelSigmaChartAff}\) (the Abel class of the arbitrary-affine carrier) is the conditional
  input to \ref{def:pic0RepresentableByOfCharts}. The degree \(n\) is a window parameter; the
  formal degree-window lemmas show that a reference divisor of degree at least \(g\) is
  available, while any consumer that insists on degree exactly \(g\) has an additional
  arithmetic/degree-pinning obligation. Only after the representation and the two seam
  antecedents are inhabited does the degree-zero Picard functor become representable and yield
  a Jacobian datum (\ref{def:jacobian_data}) --- hence, through the frozen definition
  (\ref{def:jacobian}), the Jacobian of \(C\).

  The universal family, the open-immersion chart certificates, and local surjectivity are
  distinct unproved inputs here.  The passage from a representation over a separably closed
  base to one over \(k\) is a further descent step, not addressed here.
